newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba repeats has no plans to abandon M3 targeting.
newsitem.headline: Buba repeats has no plans to abandon M3 targeting.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday that the start of 1997 had been "difficult" with respect to its main money supply indicator M3 money supply, but repeated it has no plans to switch from monetary targeting.

In its 1996 annual report, the central bank said that a statistical overhang from last year combined with high public borrowing and weak monetary capital formation had boosted M3 growth at the start of 1997.
But it made clear it stood by M3 as its main, but not sole, policy guideline.

"Despite the increased fluctuations in money supply growth which increase the need for interpretation and explanation of monetary developments, money supply orientation is still an appropriate basis for the Bundesbank's monetary policy," it said.
It added that it remained of the view that the European Central Bank, which will take over the management of European monetary policy under a single currency, should also adopt a money supply policy.
"Initial studies have confirmed that the long-term stability of money demand in the euro currency area should give the necessary basis for a money supply strategy," it added.

German M3 grew at an annualised rate of 8.3 percent in March compared with the final quarter of 1996, above a 3-1/2 to 6-1/2 percent 1997 target corridor. The March growth rate marked a slowdown from growth of 9.1 percent in February.
